quakealert_emergency_alerts
Emergency Steps & Contacts
While the ground is shaking
1. Drop
Get down on your hands and knees before the shaking knocks you down. Stay where you are. Most injuries happen to people moving between rooms or running outside.
2. Cover
Cover your head and neck with one arm. Get under a sturdy table if one is within reach, or against an interior wall away from windows, mirrors and anything tall.
3. Hold on
Hold on to your shelter and stay put until the shaking stops. If you are in bed, stay there and cover your head with a pillow.
Once the shaking stops
Expect aftershocks. The next one can arrive within seconds and can be strong enough to finish what the first one started, so keep clear of anything already damaged.
Check for gas, water and electrical damage. If you smell gas, shut the valve, open a window and do not touch light switches.
Leave only when it is safe to move, using stairs and never a lift. Check your exit route before you commit to it.
Help anyone near you who cannot move themselves before you leave the building.
Emergency numbers
112 works on any GSM network, with or without a SIM card, and is routed to the local emergency service. The numbers below it are the ones for the country this phone is currently connected to.
Dial %1$s
Your last known position
Read these coordinates out to a dispatcher if you cannot describe where you are.
No position has synced yet, so there are no coordinates to read out. Describe a landmark or a street instead.
